questions.text: The _____ is too high for it to be considered ______
questions.solution:
Fare = price of a ticket/journey; fair = reasonable / just.

"The fare is too high for it to be considered fair."

Answer: fare / fair

questions.text:
A function [latex]y(x)[/latex] is defined in the interval [0, 1] on the [latex]x-[/latex]axis as
[latex]y(x)= \left \{ \begin{matrix} 2 &if & 0 \leq x \leq \frac{1}{3} \\ 3& if& \frac{1}{3} \leq x \leq \frac{3}{4} \\ 1& if& \frac{3}{4} \leq x \leq 1 \end{matrix} \right.[/latex]
Which one of the following is the area under the curve for the interval [0, 1] on the [latex]x-[/latex]axis?
questions.solution:
Area = sum of (height [latex]\times[/latex] width) of each piece:
[latex]2\times\frac13+3\times\left(\frac34-\frac13\right)+1\times\frac14=\frac{8}{12}+\frac{15}{12}+\frac{3}{12}=\frac{26}{12}=\frac{13}{6}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{13}{6}[/latex]

questions.text:
Let [latex]r[/latex] be a root of the equation [latex]x^2+2x+6=0[/latex]
Then the value of the expression [latex](r+2)(r+3)(r+4)(r+5)[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Pair the factors: [latex](r+2)(r+5)=r^2+7r+10[/latex] and [latex](r+3)(r+4)=r^2+7r+12[/latex].

From [latex]r^2=-2r-6[/latex]: these become [latex]5r+4[/latex] and [latex]5r+6[/latex].

[latex](5r+4)(5r+6)=25r^2+50r+24=25(r^2+2r)+24=25(-6)+24=-126[/latex]

Answer: -126

questions.text:
Given below are four statements.

Statement 1: All students are inquisitive.
Statement 2: Some students are inquisitive.
Statement 3: No student is inquisitive.
Statement 4: Some students are not inquisitive.

From the given four statements, find the two statements that CANNOT BE TRUE simultaneously, assuming that there is at least one student in the class.
questions.solution:
"All students are inquisitive" and "No student is inquisitive" directly contradict each other (there is at least one student), so they can never both be true.

Every other pair can hold together (e.g. statements 2 and 4 hold when some are and some are not inquisitive).

Answer: Statement 1 and Statement 3

questions.text:
A palindrome is a word that reads the same forwards and backwards. In a game of words, a player has the following two plates painted with letters.

From the additional plates given in the options, which one of the combinations of additional plates would allow the player to construct a five-letter palindrome. The player should use all the five plates exactly once. The plates can be rotated in their plane.
questions.solution:
A 5-letter palindrome has the form X Y Z Y X, so letters must pair up around a middle letter. We already have A and D.

Option B gives R, an upside-down A and a mirrored R. Rotating the plates gives R, A, R, which makes R A D A R [latex]\text{---}[/latex] a palindrome using all 5 plates.

The other options cannot form matching pairs around a middle letter.

Answer: B
